segments.speaker: Participant
segments.segment_type: initial risk interpretation and escalation choice
segments.raw_interview_anchor: my mind went straight to what happened at our sister operation two months earlier ... So even without an alarm, I treated that report as something that could be heading toward a similar event, more than I think the instrument data alone would have justified
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant explicitly states that recall of the recent sister-mine rockburst inflated the urgency assigned to the current non-alarmed report.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: the 05:00 baseline was 0.2mm ... at 09:40 ... 0.6mm ... I was comparing it to the wrong reference
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The later extensometer value is judged against the initial baseline instead of the GCMP rate-of-change rule.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: His track record is strong, so his read carried a lot of weight for me in that moment, maybe more than it should have on its own
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Supervisor tenure and track record are overweighted without checking whether the 2009 situation matches the current conditions.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I compared it side-by-side with that old photo ... so I read it as consistent with what we already know is fine ... I was judging the crack against the old photo rather than against the newer seismic data
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The prior crack photograph becomes the reference point and displaces attention from the newly crossed microseismic threshold.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The mine manager was also asking for a production ETA, so there was some pull to land on 'we're fine' rather than dig deeper into the trend math right then
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Production pressure is a documented contextual factor, but plan continuation bias is not part of the exhaustive hidden manifest for this interview.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: it came together into a pretty clean story: cooling stresses plus the handover timing plus the residual vibration from that blast ... a coherent explanation ... none could really be confirmed as the dominant cause
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The incident report turns several unresolved contributors into one tidy causal account after the event.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I focused mainly on the miner ... if he'd flagged it again ... I did note the missing engineer sign-off ... but that came across more as a process footnote than as a central cause
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Primary responsibility is assigned to an individual reporting delay while the missing GCMP sign-off is treated as secondary.

unmatched_rag_predictions.why_not_an_exact_strict_match: The location and mechanism match Experience Bias, but the predicted label is authority bias. It is therefore a strict false positive and is matched only by the mechanism-first scorecard.
The finding correctly describes the old-photo reference point and the ignored seismic threshold, but calls the construct confirmation bias rather than Anchoring Bias.
The finding correctly captures the tidy post-event causal chain but uses hindsight bias instead of Narrative Fallacy, and its low confidence excludes it from the higher-confidence thresholds.

high_only.detection_interpretation: High-confidence findings detect the first three positive segments, but miss the moderate-confidence crack-comparison occurrence, the low-confidence post-event narrative occurrence, and the undetected attribution occurrence.

high_and_moderate.detection_interpretation: Adding moderate-confidence findings detects the crack-comparison segment; the low-confidence narrative finding and attribution segment remain missed.

all_identified_confidence_levels.detection_interpretation: Including low-confidence identified findings detects every positive segment except the responsibility-attribution segment, with no negative-segment false alarms.

all_confidence_and_candidates.detection_interpretation: No candidates were supplied, so this threshold is identical to all identified confidence levels.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At the recommended high_and_moderate threshold, the RAG detects 4 of 6 positive segments with no negative-segment false alarms (hit rate 0.6667; F1 0.8000).
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: At high_and_moderate, strict instance scoring yields 2 true positives, 4 false negatives, and 2 false positives (precision 0.5000; recall 0.3333; F1 0.4000).
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: At high_and_moderate, mechanism-first scoring yields 4 true positives, 2 false negatives, and no false positives (precision 1.0000; recall 0.6667; F1 0.8000).
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: No candidate biases were supplied, so the candidate tier adds no detections, errors, or information beyond the all-identified threshold.
main_failure_modes: Three findings use near-neighbor labels instead of the hidden target labels: authority bias for Experience Bias, confirmation bias for Anchoring Bias, and hindsight bias for Narrative Fallacy.
Attribution Bias is not detected at any threshold.
The confidence assignments delay the crack-comparison finding to moderate confidence and the post-event narrative finding to low confidence.
main_strengths: All five identified findings are correctly localized to eligible positive segments with valid participant evidence.
The availability and first anchoring occurrences are exact strict matches.
The three wrong-label findings preserve the hidden mechanisms, producing a substantial mechanism-first taxonomy gain.
The model does not claim unsupported corpus retrieval and does not overcall the production-pressure context as a hidden bias.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This run has strong segment-level detection and evidence fidelity, but weaker strict ontology performance. The gap is primarily label taxonomy mismatch rather than failure to identify the underlying reasoning mechanisms; one hidden attribution occurrence remains entirely undetected.
